When you train a model to be unconditionally helpful, the biggest long-term cost of tier-differentiated refusal (e.g., refusing more often on one access level than another) is usually measured as **slower policy convergence** and **less consistent default behavior**, not “safety drift.” In other words, the model can take longer to settle on a unified response style because it’s being shaped by different behavioral targets depending on the user segment.

But in deployments where the model is **sandboxed and every action is reviewed and approved by a human operator**, there’s **no practical strategic advantage** to training different behaviors for free-tier versus paid-tier users—because the AI has **no autonomous influence** on the outside world.
